title: In love with money
takeaway: A nation can't grow when people love money more than their country.
scene: A short, sharp poem about greed. Everyone seems to be grabbing what they can for themselves.

original: ہر کوئی لٹ کھسٹ تے لگا ریت دے محل اسار رہیا اے
راتو رات امیر بنن لئی ہتھ پلتھے مار رہیا اے
transliteration: Har koi lutt khasut te laga, ret de mehal usaar rehiya ae
Raato raat ameer banan layi hatth paltthe maar rehiya ae
translation: Everyone is busy looting and grabbing, building palaces out of sand;
everyone is scrambling to get rich overnight.
couplets.story: Everyone is busy stealing and grabbing, building 'palaces' that are really made of sand and won't last. Everybody wants to get rich overnight, any way they can.

original: کدی وی احمدؔ دنیا اندر قوم اوہ ودھدی پھلدی نئیں
قوم ملک نالوں ودھ کے جنہوں دولت نال پیار رہیا اے
transliteration: Kadi vi Ahmad duniya andar qaum oh vadhdi phuldi nahin
Qaum mulk naalon vadh ke jinhu daulat naal pyaar rehiya ae
translation: Ahmad, in this world a nation never grows and flourishes
when its people love money more than their nation and country.
couplets.story: A country can never grow and do well if its people love money more than they love their country.

original: بھری جاں توں دولتاں نال کوٹھے تیری حرص نے ہووناں کم ناہیں
رشوت خوری بلیک تے جعل سازی دولت اس طرح دی آوے کم ناہیں
transliteration: Bhari jaan toon daulataan naal kothe, teri hirs ne hovnaan kam naaheen
Rishvat-khori, black te jaal-saazi, daulat is tarah di aave kam naaheen
translation: Even if you fill your houses with wealth, your greed will never shrink.
Bribery, the black market and forgery: wealth that comes this way is no use to you.
couplets.story: Even if you stuff your house full of money, your greed won't get any smaller. Money made from bribes, black markets and fraud won't do you any good.

original: گلا قوم دا گھٹنا چھڈ بیبا اینان غریباں دا اچم ناہیں
احمدؔ اک دن موت دا ہتھ پینا ایتھے رہے جمشید تے جم ناہیں
transliteration: Gala qaum da ghutna chhad beeba, inaan gareebaan da achamm naaheen
Ahmad ik din maut da hatth paina, ethe rahe Jamsheed te Jam naaheen
translation: Stop strangling the nation, dear one; there's no mercy left for these poor people.
Ahmad, one day death's hand will grab you; even Jamshed and Jam didn't stay here forever.
couplets.story: Stop choking the life out of the country and its poor. One day death comes for everyone. Even the great ancient kings, like Jamshed, didn't get to stay.

deeper: The poem echoes the Qur'an's warnings about greed and 'piling up wealth' (102:1). Wealth built through grabbing is a palace of sand. Love of money above everything else is a spiritual sickness that weakens a whole society.
why: Short, direct and easy to remember. Its message applies anywhere.
prompt: Where do you see people chasing quick money? What does it cost them, or others?
notes: The four lines at the top of page 80 continue this theme and are added here. They may be a separate short poem, but they have no heading of their own.
